title: Wall MSSI as the origin of the LZ event: the mismodelling factor required and what the sidebands allow
question: By what factor k must the modelled wall-MSSI rate be too low for a wall MSSI to be a likely origin of the 248 keV event, and do LZ's own MSSI sideband counts allow such a factor?
headline_result: Wall MSSI needs k >= 620 (410-930) for a 10% chance of one event in the candidate's neighbourhood, while the six wall sideband bins (2 obs vs 3.23 pred) give k_ML = 0.62 and k < 1.64 at 95%: required/allowed ~ 380; wall MSSI is not a viable explanation.
key_numbers: k_ML=0.62; k<1.36 (90%), <1.64 (95%) LR, 1.95 Bayes; science-only 2.15; extreme misclassification 3.6; f_nb=0.035 (0.024-0.053); Fig.5 digitisation total 0.01053 vs 0.0106; k_req(10%)=22 ROI / 619 neighbourhood, k_req(50%)=144 / 4070; P(>=1 nb | k=1.64)=2.8e-4; Bayes factor k-free vs k=1 0.93-1.4; topology suppression 1e-4-0.04; f_pos 1e-4-0.12 -> k_req >= 5e3; veto untagged 6+-2% = +-33% on 0.0048
model_or_mechanism: Common scale factor k on wall-MSSI rate (charge-dead-layer geometry); Poisson likelihood on supplementary MSSI comparison table; Fig. 5 pixel digitisation for the neighbourhood fraction; Compton kinematics + LXe attenuation for the 12 keV + 77 keV topology
stance: supports DM interpretation (weakly, by elimination of wall MSSI only)
